title: Ocarina of Time's Z-Targeting Came From a Ninja Show in Kyoto
hook:
In the mid nineties three Zelda developers ducked into a theme park ninja show to escape the heat, and walked out with Z-targeting. Ocarina of Time's remake hits Switch 2 this Thursday, November 5. Will you be playing it again?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know the lock on targeting in Ocarina of Time was inspired by a ninja stage show at a theme park in Kyoto? In the nineties, Nintendo was building its first three D Zelda and wanted sword fights that felt like samurai movies. So three members of the team, including the designer Yoshiaki Koizumi, visited Toei Kyoto Studio Park on a hot summer day. They wandered into a playhouse mostly to escape the heat, and caught a ninja show. A lone samurai stood surrounded by ninja, yet the enemies never attacked all at once. One stepped forward while the others circled and waited their turn. Koizumi realized that was the only way one hero could believably beat a crowd. That idea became Z targeting. Lock on to one enemy, and the rest of the room holds back. Another team member watched a ninja swing a sickle on a chain and imagined an invisible chain between Link and his target. The targeting marker started as a plain triangle, until Koizumi turned it into a fairy and called it the Fairy Navigation System. The team shortened that to Navi. Ocarina of Time released in nineteen ninety eight, and this Thursday, November fifth, a full remake lands on Switch two. Will you be playing it again? Follow for more gaming history.
